name: Pan-European nationalism
summary: Pan-European nationalism holds that the peoples of Europe form one nation that should have one government and be independent of both the United States and the Soviet Union. The postwar movement was an anti-liberal and anti-communist far right: its main strands, Mosley's Europe a Nation, Yockey's Imperium and Thiriart's Jeune Europe, agree on union, an armed third force, a self-sufficient Europe-Africa bloc and separation of Europeans from non-Europeans, and differ on democracy, class and the Soviet Union.
scope: The nationalism of the European nation itself, 1945 to the 1970s: Oswald Mosley's Europe a Nation (Union Movement, Europe: Faith and Plan 1958), the 1962 Declaration of Venice of the National Party of Europe (signed by Union Movement, Jeune Europe, Reichspartei and others), Yockey's Imperium and the European Liberation Front's Proclamation of London, Thiriart's Jeune Europe and the 1950-51 Rome/Malmo programme of the European Social Movement. Positions stated by one strand only are left null, or are a split where another strand states the opposite; the economic and social programmes of the parties that carried it count only where these texts state them as part of the European cause. It excludes pro-EU federalism and later Eurosceptic or Identitarian movements.

notes: Strands: Mosley's Europe a Nation (a unitary elected government with national parliaments for social and cultural matters, free elections, state economic leadership, racial separation); Yockey (an Imperium that abolishes the nations, rejects democracy and liberalism, and tactically favoured the USSR); Thiriart (a unitary European state led by a revolutionary elite, free enterprise as a means, independent unions, anti-Soviet in 1964 and later national-communist); the Malmo programme (a federal European Nation of equal states, Christian, free elections, equality of white and colored peoples). Where these disagree the answer is 0 at low confidence; positions stated by one strand only are null. Themes searched: economy, government, society, world, liberty, culture, ecology, technology, means, globalism. Positions on ecology, technology, gender, drugs, policing and most economic policy are not stated in these texts. Blocked: Britannica's Mosley entry and academia.edu (Cloudflare challenge), Taylor and Francis article on the European far right's geopolitics (403), Charles University thesis on Mosley's Europe (no connection); Thiriart's English translation and Mosley's 'The Alternative' (1947), 'Mosley: Right or Wrong?' and 'My Life' were not available as full text and the main gap is Mosley's postwar pamphlets and the Union Movement's own programmes. Review (2026-10-30): unions-good, collective-bargaining, farm-price-support and regulate-corporations nulled under the scope rule, as in arab-nationalism.
